title: Build compatibility matrix, migration fixtures, and release CI
description:
## Objective
Make contract evolution safe before the first tagged release.

## Scope
- Cross-language fixture runner
- Previous-reader/current-writer compatibility cases
- Migration fixture convention and skeleton migrator registry
- Schema lint, docs generation, package build, and release checks

## Boundaries and risks
- Preserve canonical workspace and contract ownership boundaries.
- Add deterministic tests for failure paths, cancellation, and restart where applicable.
- Do not hide a material downgrade or destructive migration behind a fallback.
design: Phase: release. Implement behind typed ports and versioned contracts. Keep diagnostics machine-readable and user-actionable. Update module documentation and fixtures together with behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] One command runs schema, TypeScript, Python, and compatibility suites
- [ ] CI fails on ungenerated bindings or undocumented breaking changes
- [ ] v0.1.0 artifacts and changelog can be produced from a clean checkout
- [ ] Unit/integration tests cover success and relevant failure paths.
- [ ] Public contract and operator/contributor documentation are updated.
notes: Compatibility/release task covers every catalog family and enforces docs/compatibility-policy.md.

title: Ship v1alpha1 cross-module production contracts
description:
## Objective
Define and release the language-neutral schemas and generated bindings that let independently versioned studio modules exchange workspace files, commands, jobs, and events without drift.

## Delivery boundary
Complete all child beads to produce the module's MVP release. Cross-module integration uses released contracts and fakes before depending on live paid or hardware services.

## Planning rule
Child dependencies encode implementation order. A child is complete only when its acceptance criteria and tests are satisfied, not when code merely exists.
design: Canonical JSON Schema is the source; generated bindings must never become hand-edited alternatives. Compatibility is proved with fixtures in TypeScript and Python.
acceptance_criteria: All child beads are closed; module README and generated/operator documentation match behavior; clean checkout passes build, test, lint, contract, and release checks; no known P0/P1 defect remains.
